external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: Deployed sensor on a customer site, outside the operator's physical control. Publishes readings and self-installs firmware.
external_entities.source_excerpt: They are outside our physical control — a technician can be standing next to one with a laptop.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: Person who services deployed nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: Internal staff member reading fleet dashboards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: Internet-exposed MQTT broker on GKE; authenticates nodes against the registry and forwards accepted readings.
processes.source_excerpt: an MQTT broker we run on GKE and expose to the internet because the nodes dial in from anywhere

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: Python Pub/Sub consumer that normalizes readings and loads them into the lake.
processes.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: Firestore collection holding the fleet pre-shared key check and each node's customer assignment.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: BigQuery dataset of normalized readings, including site addresses and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: Cloud Storage bucket the nodes poll for firmware images. Public read.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The bucket is public read, because making the nodes authenticate to it was awkward.

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: The broker the gateway publishes accepted readings onto and the normalizer consumes them from.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: Node publishes sensor readings to the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Nodes authenticate to the broker with a pre-shared key. The key is per fleet, not per device. Nobody has rotated it since deployment.
data_flows.authentication: fleet-wide pre-shared key, shared by every device and never rotated
data_flows.data_description: sensor readings tagged with a device identifier

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: Gateway checks the presented key and resolves the node's customer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.
data_flows.data_description: device identifier, key material, customer assignment

data_flows.name: load readings
data_flows.description: Normalizer writes readings into the lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll firmware
data_flows.description: Node polls for a new firmware image and installs what it finds.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image and install what they find
data_flows.authentication: none; the bucket is public read

data_flows.name: local service session
data_flows.description: Technician attaches to a node's serial console on site.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console. I don't know what authentication that console has, if any.

data_flows.name: query dashboards
data_flows.description: Operator reads fleet dashboards over BigQuery.
data_flows.source_excerpt: look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The gateway publishes accepted readings onto the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The normalizer consumes readings from the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub and picked up by the telemetry normalizer

trust_boundaries.name: field network
trust_boundaries.description: Customer sites where nodes and technicians sit; outside the operator's physical control.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: They are outside our physical control

trust_boundaries.name: ingest edge
trust_boundaries.description: Internet-exposed ingest tier: the broker, the registry it reads, and the firmware bucket.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: expose to the internet because the nodes dial in from anywhere

trust_boundaries.name: analytics core
trust_boundaries.description: Internal analytics network holding the normalizer and the lake.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Staff network from which operators reach dashboards.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO

assumptions.assumption: The firmware bucket accepts unauthenticated reads from anywhere.
assumptions.basis: Described as "public read" and polled by devices that hold no credential for it.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake holds personal data about customer sites.
assumptions.basis: Stated to contain "site addresses and occupancy patterns", described as customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake holds confidential data under the scheme in prompts/extract.md.
assumptions.basis: The source says the lake has "site addresses and occupancy patterns" in it and calls it customer data. Both describe identifiable customer premises and when they are occupied, so disclosure harms the customers described.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub sits in the ingest edge rather than the analytics network.
assumptions.basis: The source places the normalizer "in our analytics network" and places the broker nowhere. It associates the broker with the gateway's onward hop — "Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub" — so it takes the gateway's zone. Either placement leaves exactly one crossing on this path.

assumptions.assumption: field technician's trust_zone is boundary:field-network, which the schema requires and no source states.
assumptions.basis: Servicing nodes over a local console implies being where the nodes are. No sentence places it. The model's zone is a reasonable reading of the architecture, not something the source says.

assumptions.assumption: telemetry normalizer's exposure is internal, which the schema requires and no source states.
assumptions.basis: No sentence states its reachability. Sitting in an internal network implies it, which is an inference rather than a statement.

assumptions.assumption: device registry's trust_zone is boundary:ingest-edge, which the schema requires and no source states.
assumptions.basis: No sentence places it. The model's zone is a reasonable reading of the architecture, not something the source says.

assumptions.assumption: telemetry lake's trust_zone is boundary:analytics-core, which the schema requires and no source states.
assumptions.basis: No sentence places it. The model's zone is a reasonable reading of the architecture, not something the source says.

assumptions.assumption: firmware bucket's trust_zone is boundary:ingest-edge, which the schema requires and no source states.
assumptions.basis: Public read makes its placement arguable as well as unstated. No sentence places it. The model's zone is a reasonable reading of the architecture, not something the source says.

assumptions.assumption: sensor node's trust_zone is boundary:field-network, which the schema requires and no source states.
assumptions.basis: Installation at customer sites is explicit; a single field network is not. The model's zone is a reasonable grouping of those sites, not something the source says.

assumptions.assumption: device gateway's trust_zone is boundary:ingest-edge, which no source states.
assumptions.basis: The quote names GKE and internet exposure, not an ingest-edge network or membership in it. The zone is the model's own grouping of the ingest path.
